response: Anorectal endosonography is a valuable diagnostic tool in the evaluation of dyschésia. This ultrasonographic technique can provide detailed images of the anal sphincter and muscles, allowing for the assessment of their relaxation during defecation movements. In many cases, anorectal endosonography has demonstrated incomplete or even absent relaxation of the anal sphincter and the muscle puborectalis in patients with dyschésia, which is a hallmark of "pelvic floor dyssynergia" or "anismus". This can help confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.
